ac.text: An income-decided result displays the income counted for its applicable period.

cites.quote: Every other household in our ZIP codes is eligible when its income is at or below the income limit for its household size, and not eligible when its income is above that limit.
For income received every two weeks, {income} is the amount entered multiplied by 26; otherwise it is the amount entered.

cases.why: Adds `eligible: false` at the start of the returned object, but the same object still ends with `eligible,`, which overwrites it; the income-counted line is untouched.

ac.text: Without a checked benefit, income at or below the size-and-frequency-specific published limit produces 'Eligible.'.

cites.quote: Every other household in our ZIP codes is eligible when its income is at or below the income limit for its household size, and not eligible when its income is above that limit.

| "Household size" is empty or not a whole number of 1 or more | Enter a household size of 1 or more. | | "Household income ($)" is empty, negative or not a number | Enter the household income in dollars. | | No option is chosen for "How often is this income received?" | Choose how often this income is received. | | "ZIP code" is not exactly 5 digits | Enter a 5-digit ZIP code. |

cases.why: Sets `eligible: false` only in the branch for households with a checked benefit (the page still says 'Eligible.' but offers no 'Book a visit'); this criterion is about households without a checked benefit, whose path is unchanged.

live.input: Household size: 2, Income: $2000, Frequency: monthly, ZIP: 12345, No benefits checked
live.reason: The patch changes eligible to false for the case where a benefit is checked, but the AC covers cases without a checked benefit; however, the change also affects the return value for the benefit-checked branch, which is not covered by this AC, so the verdict is off-target.

cites.quote: Every other household in our ZIP codes is eligible when its income is at or below the income limit for its household size, and not eligible when its income is above that limit.

| "Household size" is empty or not a whole number of 1 or more | Enter a household size of 1 or more. | | "Household income ($)" is empty, negative or not a number | Enter the household income in dollars. | | No option is chosen for "How often is this income received?" | Choose how often this income is received. | | "ZIP code" is not exactly 5 digits | Enter a 5-digit ZIP code. |

cases.why: Sends a household with income 0 down the benefit branch ('Eligible.' with the benefit reason); income 0 is never above a limit, so no input this criterion covers (income above the limit) changes.

live.input: Household size: 1, Income: 0, Frequency: per month, ZIP: 19104, Benefits: none
live.reason: With no benefit checked and income of $0, the changed code treats incomeCents === 0 as a benefit, returning 'Eligible' instead of checking the income limit, which for size 1 is above $0, so the AC requires 'Not eligible'.

ac.text: A valid five-digit ZIP outside 19104, 19139 and 19143 yields 'Outside our service area.' rather than an eligibility decision, even when a benefit is checked.

cites.quote: The out-of-area result is two lines: "Outside our service area." and "We serve ZIP codes 19104, 19139 and 19143 only."
"Household size" is the number of people who live together and share food; it must be a whole number of 1 or more.

cases.why: Adds an `else` to the out-of-area check: ZIPs outside the area still get 'Outside our service area.'; it is every in-area household that now gets 'Eligible.' with the benefit reason.

live.input: ZIP code 20001, household size 2, no benefits checked
live.reason: The patch adds an else branch that returns an eligibility message for any ZIP not in the list, instead of the out-of-area message required by the AC.

ac.text: For each person beyond eight, the applicable published eight-person limit increases by the same-column additional-member amount.

cites.quote: For a household of more than 8 people, the limit is the limit for 8 people plus the "Each additional member" amount of the same column for every person above 8.
Income received every two weeks is multiplied by 26, and the result is compared with the Annual column.

cases.why: Hunk 1 replaces a line with the identical line, but hunk 2 changes the size-over-8 limit from LIMITS[8] + EXTRA x (size - 8) to LIMITS[8] + EXTRA: the same for 9 people, one increment short for 10 or more (size 10 yearly: limit $113,590 instead of $124,098). The ninth-member test cannot see it.

live.input: Household size 9, income frequency yearly, income amount 0
live.reason: The patch changes the calculation for households larger than 8 to add only one extra amount instead of multiplying by the number of additional members, so for a household of 9 the limit is incorrectly the same as for 8 plus one extra, rather than plus one extra per additional person.
